newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil oilworkers to stop work for two hours Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil oilworkers to stop work for two hours Thurs.

text.p: Brazilian oilworkers will stop work for two hours on September 26 as part of a campaign for higher wages and job security, but production will not be affected, a union spokeswoman said.
And, despite deadlock in talks between the Single Oilworkers Federation (FUP) and state monopoly Petrobras possibility of an all-out strike is not yet imminent, the FUP spokeswoman said.
"It's not on the agenda yet," she said. "For the time being we are seeking to negotiate."
Workers will not work for the first two hours of their shifts on Thursday "to send a message to Petrobras that they want their demands to be negotiated," the spokeswoman said.
The action will coincide with a strike by Brazilian bank workers and a general strike in Argentina.
FUP says Brazil's 50,000 oilworkers are entitled to pay rises of about 40 percent and is willing to negotiate less but not as low as the eight percent offered by Petrobras.
The unions are also holding out for a clause guaranteeing the job security of workers in a collective contract which is negotiated annually.

Brazilian oilworkers have gone on strike three times in the last two years over pay and benefits and in opposition to the government's economic policies. The strikes forced Brazil to increase imports of refined products, in particular diesel and liquid petroleum gas, forcing prices up on international markets.
